text:
erin: Heads-up — thinking about consolidating telemetry attribute storage. Instead of denormalized attr tables per-event-type we want a compact attributes column (jsonb) + small attribute index table to speed filters. Goal: reduce table count, speed common console queries, and simplify rollouts for new event kinds.
kevin: Curious on perf tradeoffs — jsonb can be fast for reads but index strategy matters. do we lose cardinality metrics? :eyes: 
dave: Main risk is backfills and index builds. large existing tenant has 10B rows; building a GIN index will eat IO and bloat. Need nonblocking plan.
maria: Agree. Proposal sketch: (1) add new nullable jsonb `attrs_compact` to telemetry.events (no locks), (2) dual-write new events to both old attr tables and attrs_compact behind a feature flag, (3) create a small attributes lookup table for heavy-filter keys (key, value, event_id) that we can index btree on (key, value) for frequent filters, (4) backfill older rows in chunks with a job that streams and writes to attrs_compact, (5) switch console queries to prefer attrs_compact via view fallback.
josh: That seems sane. Two questions: how do we keep quota accounting and ingestion pipeline compatible during the period of dual-write? and how long do we expect the backfill to take?
erin: Quota accounting lives in the same event envelope but we already have a compact token_count column; dual-write won't touch quotas. Backfill speed depends on chunk size and tenant rate-limits; for 10B rows estimate ~2-3 weeks with moderate parallelism unless we use snapshotting + COPY.
kevin: If we use COPY for chunks, we can avoid per-row inserts. Idea: export PK + attrs -> transform -> COPY into a temp table then update via JOIN. But updates on 10B rows still expensive. Maybe create a new table events_v2, populate it, then swap with a view? Hard with FK constraints.
dave: I want a nonblocking incremental backfill runner — something like this pseudo-psql pipeline:```sql
-- pseudo
CREATE TEMP TABLE chunk(pk bigint, attrs jsonb);
COPY chunk FROM '/tmp/chunk.csv';
UPDATE telemetry.events e
SET attrs_compact = c.attrs
FROM chunk c
WHERE e.pk = c.pk;
```
instead of updating whole table at once we run many parallel chunk jobs with throttle. Also we should run ANALYZE on each updated range.
platform-bot: NOTE: creating new column on large table will perform a metadata-only commit on modern Postgres versions if added as NULLABLE. Confirming engine: Aurora Postgres 13.4 — add column is cheap.
maria: Good catch. Index plan: create partial indexes for the most common keys to keep index size reasonable. Eg:CREATE INDEX ON telemetry.attr_index (key, value) WHERE key IN ('route_id', 'tenant_id');
josh: For console dashboards we need deterministic query compatibility. Suggest creating a view telemetry.event_attrs that coalesces between legacy join and attrs_compact:```sql
CREATE VIEW telemetry.event_attrs AS
SELECT e.*, COALESCE(e.attrs_compact, jsonb_object_agg(a.key, a.value)) as attrs
FROM telemetry.events e
LEFT JOIN telemetry.attrs a ON a.event_id = e.pk
GROUP BY e.pk;
```
erin: That view approach lets us flip console to the new path behind a feature flag and also supports gradual rollbacks. But note jsonb_object_agg requires grouping which could be heavy if used naively; we'll only use it as fallback for reads in canary mode.
kevin: Rollback plan: keep dual-write for at least 2 weeks after switching console traffic. If we see query regressions revert console to view that prefers legacy joins. Also keep a small sampling stream of events into long-term storage to run offline quality checks.
dave: Operational runbook items: - rate-limit backfill per-tenant - monitor bloat and index build metrics - pre-create new indexes concurrently: CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY ... - set maintenance_window for heavy ops - ensure backups before swap - have kill-switch to disable backfill.
maria: Need ownership: @kevin for indexing/backfill orchestration, @dave for console query changes and rollback runbook, @erin for schema design and flags.
analytics-ci: added test:telemetry/compact_attrs to CI that validates dual-write consistency on staged sample.
josh: One more thing — quota and billing analytics depend on attribute-level counts for some customers. We'll add a small compatibility lambda that emits aggregated counts from attrs_compact into existing billing tables during migration.
erin: Final checklist I propose: 1) schema add attrs_compact (nullable) — low risk 2) dual-write behind flag + CI tests 3) deploy console view that prefers attrs_compact but falls back 4) small-index table + partial indexes for hot keys 5) staged backfill with chunked COPY and ANALYZE 6) canary traffic (10% tenants) for 48-72h 7) promote and remove legacy attr tables after 60 days of no issues (with careful deprecation notices)
kevin: LGTM. I'll draft backfill job and share resource estimates. :shipit:
dave: I'll prep dashboard queries and a revert script.
maria: I'll add the feature flag toggles in the config and update docs.
erin: thanks all. I'll write the RFC and schedule sync tomorrow. :thumbsup:
